observed: Both Intel Clang versions preserve the entire ordinary decoder text and relocations, but decline the intended generic tail transfer. Clang14 emits one push/call/return; Clang18 saves R9, adjusts RSP and emits calls to both destinations. The selector widens the narrow opcode and stack boolean arguments before those calls. AArch64 already emits two tail branches.
hypothesis: Require tail transfer at the two same-signature selector returns where Clang supports musttail. Original argument types, calling convention and pointer lifetimes match; no local address escapes. Preserve the existing fallback on older Clang versions without the attribute.
gate: Keep R1434 exact ordinary-code proof and no-stack/no-call selector gate unchanged. Compiler rejection or any remaining frame blocks instruction-cost and native qualification.
